name: Poorly Differentiated Thymic Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma morphology in thymic tissue
Positive immunohistochemical staining for neuroendocrine markers such as chromogranin A, synaptophysin, and CD56
Radiologic evidence of anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymic origin
Exclusion of metastatic neuroendocrine carcinoma from other primary sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive neuroendocrine immunohistochemistry and imaging consistent with thymic origin, excluding metastatic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary correlation including pathology, radiology, and clinical findings

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Often asymptomatic initially, detected incidentally or by mass effect
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome due to ectopic ACTH secretion
pathognomonic.notes: May present with characteristic metabolic disturbances
searchTerms: excess cortisol due to tumor hormone

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or mass effect
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.notes: Due to vascular compression by tumor

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: voice changes due to recurrent laryngeal nerve

occasional.notes: Rare ectopic insulin-like growth factor secretion
May be related to tumor necrosis or cytokine release

rare.symptomName: Superior mediastinal syndrome with facial edema
searchTerms: swelling of face from upper chest vein blockage
facial edema due to mediastinal compression
superior mediastinal syndrome with facial swelling

rare.notes: Autoimmune neuromuscular disorder associated with neuroendocrine tumors
searchTerms: autoimmune muscle weakness related to cancer

rare.notes: Clubbing and periostitis secondary to tumor

laboratory: Elevated serum ACTH in cases with ectopic Cushing syndrome
Hyponatremia and hypokalemia due to paraneoplastic syndromes
Elevated neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and chromogranin A levels
imaging: CT scan showing anterior mediastinal mass with invasive features
PET-CT demonstrating hypermetabolic activity of thymic lesion
genetic: Frequent mutations in TP53 and RB1 genes
Loss of heterozygosity at chromosome 3p and 13q regions
other: Histopathology showing small to intermediate-sized cells with high mitotic rate
Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56

distinguishingFeatures: Thymoma typically shows epithelial cell proliferation without neuroendocrine markers
Primary lung lesion identified on imaging
Different clinical presentation with predominant pulmonary symptoms
Immunohistochemistry may overlap but clinical context differs
Lymphoid cell markers positive on immunophenotyping

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
Paraneoplastic endocrine syndromes such as Cushing syndrome
references: Travis WD, Brambilla E, Burke AP, Marx A, Nicholson AG. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. 4th ed. IARC; 2015.
